newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks look for firm footing after slump.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks look for firm footing after slump.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market is likely to attempt to reorganise itself in the coming week, trying to find firm footing after slumping below the 20,000 level on Friday for the first time in three months, brokers said.

"After the benchmark skidded past the 20,000 threshold, the next resistance is pegged at 19,500 to 19,600, which is quite far away," an official at an investment trust affiliated with a "Big Four" brokerage said.
A futures trader with a middle-sized brokerage said the market was likely to be sensitive to the the 20,000 level for the Nikkei and 1,500 for the broader TOPIX index.

"On both Thursday and Friday (last week) stocks struggled higher in the 11th hour, erasing some of the earlier loses," he said. "But the rises were forced by dealers and did not reflect actual demand, so market sentiment is still pretty sour."
However, some brokers said that pension and public funds were likely to cushion falls, especially below 20,000.

"For the rest of the year, buying from investors such as public pension funds will support the market," Shinichi Ichikawa, a strategist at Credit Lyonnais Securities, told Reuters Financial Television.
On Friday, the Nikkei 225 ended 159.81 points, or 0.78 percent, down at 20,341, after tumbling as low as 19,951.69, jolted by the Dow's steep fall on Thursday of nearly 100 points.
Some brokers said that bouts of weakness in Globex S&P 500 futures contracts were also contributing to the jitters.
"The Tokyo market is very sensitive to moves in New York, especially after the recent Greenspan comments," said Tadahiro Kamogawa, Yamaichi Securities general manager.

U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan rattled markets worldwide earlier this month with a warning about "irrational exuberance" in financial markets. The comment was taken as a hint that the U.S. Federal Reserve Board might resort to higher interest rates to slow the markets' ascent.
The warning forced the Nikkei average to plunge 667.20 to end at 20,276.70 on December 6. posting the largest one-day drop this year.
Brokers said the Tokyo stock market was likely to keep an eagle eye on the U.S. market, searching for directional cues.
Market sources estimated that the Nikkei average was likely to stay in the 19,800 to 20,800 range in the coming week.
